title: The Nine Situations
coreMove: Change conduct as the human pressure of the ground changes, especially when danger can create unity or panic.
sourcePressure: The source names nine grounds, prescribes different actions for each, emphasizes solidarity deeper in hostile country, seized valuables, desperate ground, shuai-jan responsiveness, Wu and Yueh cooperating in a storm, and Marquis Wu mourning his troops.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the nine situations into a static taxonomy instead of pressure-sensitive leadership.

sourceAnchors.name: the Ch'ang mountains
sourceAnchors.detail: The shuai-jan is described as a creature from the Ch'ang mountains whose head, tail, and middle answer attacks as one body.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A team under pressure should answer like the shuai-jan: touch one part and the whole body knows.

sourceAnchors.name: the men of Wu and Yueh in the same boat
sourceAnchors.detail: Enemies from Wu and Yueh are said to help each other when caught together crossing a river in a storm.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Shared danger can turn old rivals into two hands on the same oar.

sourceAnchors.name: Marquis Wu
sourceAnchors.detail: After his troops were annihilated, he is found in his chariot with sword drawn and weeping for men who did not return.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Marquis Wu's tears belong beside his error: leadership has to count the lives that pay for bad ground.

hook: A battlefield metaphor imported into a modern office before the actual choice is visible
A generic sentence about strategy being planning under pressure
counterintuition: The obvious move is not always best; the opposite move is smarter
Winning is not about strength but about strategy
tryThisNow: Set a timer and think about your next battle
Write down your goal and one obstacle
examples: manager staring at a spreadsheet with a coffee cup

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches repeated phrases but not the deeper template of timestamp plus named protagonist plus prop plus decision that makes six examples feel like one example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a direct question, a tactical aside, a second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital merger team integrating two rival wards
exampleSpecs.audience: nursing director after a merger announcement
exampleSpecs.stakes: old loyalties could fracture patient handoffs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: They do not need another speech; they need the same storm, Sophie says, then pairs rival charge nurses on the one handoff neither ward can manage alone.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two ward boards with different color codes

exampleSpecs.domain: startup running out of runway before a regulatory deadline
exampleSpecs.audience: founder with six weeks of cash
exampleSpecs.stakes: panic could scatter engineers into pet fixes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 1:30 a.m., Sam removes side projects from the board and makes the deadline visible enough that the team stops bargaining with dispersive ground.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a runway chart taped over a whiteboard

exampleSpecs.domain: fire crew entering a warehouse with one exit route
exampleSpecs.audience: incident commander at a chemical storage fire
exampleSpecs.stakes: wrong pressure could trap firefighters inside
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: When does closing the escape path create focus, and when does it create a body count?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: chemical placards beside a roll-up door

exampleSpecs.domain: peacekeeping logistics team negotiating a mountain checkpoint
exampleSpecs.stakes: a blocked road could isolate clinics for days
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Loose gravel slides under the lead truck as Marit treats the checkpoint as intersecting ground and calls allies before anyone argues at the barrier.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: loose gravel beneath a convoy tire

exampleSpecs.domain: professional kitchen after a freezer failure before service
exampleSpecs.audience: executive chef with two rival sous-chefs
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team can save service only if rivalry collapses into one response
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Warm air rolls from the walk-in as Javier gives each rival half the salvage plan so head and tail answer together.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: warm air from a walk-in freezer

exampleSpecs.domain: research vessel caught between storm and equipment failure
exampleSpecs.audience: chief scientist leading a mixed crew
exampleSpecs.stakes: scientists and deck crew must cooperate or lose the whole expedition
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Hiroshi one snapped sampling cable to stop managing departments and start managing the single boat they were all inside.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a snapped cable across a wet deck

skillTargets: use shared danger to create unity without manipulation
diagnose when pressure produces courage or panic

tryThisNowSpec: Classify your team's current ground, then change one leadership behavior to match it: do not use home-ground persuasion on desperate-ground pressure.
